property.name: lines
property.value: Don't finish them in the green. Drag them onto dry ground first. Learned that one the hard way. | The Lady of House Vey keeps the green for the King. If anyone can pull that thing out of you, it's her. Whether you'd live through it is another matter. | Me? Never took the Gift. The dead don't seem to notice me. One of the few perks of the job. | My grandfather swore a king walked into the Sinking Fields and never walked out. There is a pit down there, between the dead trees on the south bank - deeper than the others, with a crowned stone at its lip. I have never had a reason to find out where it goes.

property.name: lines
property.value: The only quiet patch in the Vale. Babes who died before they could drink. Not one of them has stood up. | Funny. The Choir calls these the lost ones.

property.name: card_sub
property.value: PRECENTOR OF THE CHOIR

property.name: intro_line1
property.value: The Nameless. You silenced my bells - and I heard every one of them fall quiet.

property.name: intro_line2
property.value: Seven hundred years the Choir has sung for Him in the dark. Tonight, at last, the hymn has its verse.

property.name: intro_line3
property.value: Give me the Eye, and the Choir will lift Him up at last.

property.name: relic_hint
property.value: The ears sink into you, and the world grows loud: Afterecho, Discord and Forewarning - three mantras attuned as one.

property.name: relic_say
property.value: So that's how he heard me coming... Every bell. Every step.

property.name: relic_text
property.value: Something falls from under the Precentor's hood - a pair of withered ears on a cord, older than any bell in the Vale. As they leave him, they begin to glow blue.

property.name: depart_text
property.value: Down. Then further down.

property.name: open_text
property.value: With his last breath, Morrow tears the Requiem Door open. Red light pours out of it.

property.name: intro_line1
property.value: So this is the Nameless. My King would pay a great deal for you.

property.name: intro_line2
property.value: House Vey kept this vale before their Hierophant learned to write. We kept it with blood.

property.name: intro_line3
property.value: Kneel, and I will cut the Eye out of you gently. You will hardly miss the rest.

property.name: intro_line2

property.name: intro_line3

property.name: text
property.value:
Weighted down with a stone on the watch's supply barrel.

To the Lychgate watch.

A man came up out of the pump works drain. No family, no Naming, no name. He carries what the Choir has waited four hundred years for. He is to be taken ALIVE and brought to the Precentor.

Keep the bells ringing. The Precentor hears what the bells hear - he will know where the man is before you see him.

Any man who drinks his blood or wastes it answers to Morrow. - Sergeant of the Lantern

property.name: title

property.name: text
property.value:
Pages torn from the Book of Names, blown out across the flagstones.

...every child of the Vale, in its twelfth year, is brought to the Chapel to drink of the Font. Only then is its name written in the Book of Names.

A name written is a soul bound. A soul bound is a soul kept.

- Chapter of the Naming, verse 4

property.name: text
property.value:
Small crosses ring the old tree. Each reads only: "Unnamed. At rest."

A scrap tucked under a stone, in the Sexton's hand:
Babes who died before the Naming. The Choir says they are lost. Funny - it's the only quiet patch in the Vale. - A.

property.name: title
property.value: Field of the Unnamed

property.name: text
property.value:
The vintage thins each year. Tonight we dig up Uncle.

Grandmother Isolde still sleeps below the old crypt. We do not dig there. We do not even knock.

The King's riders came again tonight. They want the thing the drain-man carries - for the King's collection, they said, and whole. Grandmother says if she brings it to him, he will lift her up into the light at last. She has been promised that before.

property.name: text

The Eternal King gives, and his Gift answers.

The serf drank, and worked without rest. The soldier drank, and did not fall. The noble drank of the older water,

and did not die.

Give thanks for the Gift. Ask nothing more of it.

property.value: Moonlight floods the glass, and the picture is not the one in the prayer books. No glory, no gold. A figure lies on its back above dark water, and many hands reach over it - each hand wearing the ring of a great House. White birds rise from the water. Close to the figure's chest, one hand wears no ring at all.

property.name: text
property.value:
A reliquary case far older than the Chapel's pews, its lid stamped with the crown of Vael. Whoever brought it here brought it a long way, and in a hurry: one hinge is torn half off.

The velvet inside is pressed into hollows. One long and ridged, like a string of knuckles. Two small and curled, like shells. One round.

All of them empty. Dust has settled in each of them, and in nothing else.

property.name: title
property.value: Reliquary of the Crown

property.name: text
property.value:
A small case of black lacquer left on the crypt step - new, its gold still bright, the King's seal on the lid. Inside, a single round hollow lined with fresh red velvet. It is about the size of an eye.

A card is tucked into the lid:

To be filled in the Vale, and carried to the capital by a Vey hand. Not to be opened on the road.
 - by order of the Crown
